copy.title: [Heated product type: jacket/vest/gloves], [battery or heat feature: e.g. 3 heat zones, 7.4V battery], [second feature: e.g. water-resistant, washable], for [men/women], [colour], [size range]
copy.title_example: Heated Jacket with 3 Heat Zones and Battery Pack, Water-Resistant, for Men, Black, Sizes S-3XL
desc: Open with one line stating the product type, who it is for (men or women) and the key spec, e.g. 'Men's heated vest with 4 heat zones and a rechargeable battery pack.' No adjectives without a number or fact.

Then 4-6 checkable facts from the supplier spec sheet, one per line: heat zones and where they sit, heat settings and temperatures, battery voltage and capacity, run time per setting, charge time, shell and fill material, washing instructions, size range, what is in the box.
fact_types: Number and location of heat zones (chest, back, pockets, hands, fingers)
Battery voltage, capacity (mAh) and whether the battery is included
Run time on low, medium and high, and charge time
Shell and insulation material, water resistance, and washing instructions
Size range and fit, with a men's or women's size chart
faq: Is the battery included, and how long does it last on each heat setting?
Can I wash it, and do I need to remove the battery or heating elements first?
Can I wear it in rain or snow, and can I take the battery on a plane?
voice: Plain and practical: state heat zones, hours and voltage as numbers, not as 'warm' or 'cozy'.
Write for someone standing in the cold: say where the heat sits and how long it lasts on each setting.
Same structure for men's and women's listings; only fit, size range and zone placement change. No exclamation marks, no emoji.
applied: User parameters: none given, so the default Heated Apparel pattern was used.
Shopper split men/women was built into the title, site title and size chart fact, as it is a main search term in this niche.

Every spec in the patterns is a slot to be filled only from the supplier spec sheet; battery run times, water resistance and wash instructions are left out where the sheet does not state them. FAQ answers must use the sheet's numbers and the store's policy, and airline battery rules should only be quoted if the sheet or policy gives them.
